editorial:
Imagine trying to pitch a TV show where every single episode is just a story about how you made the episode before it. That is exactly the wild idea Caveh Zahedi pushes on a small arts group in Brooklyn. You get to follow him as he drags a group of quirky, stressed-out indie filmmakers into his chaotic world. The vibe is very loose and feels like you are just hanging out with a group of friends who are way in over their heads. It is a funny look at how ego and bad planning can turn a simple project into a total mess.

What really makes this work is the acting, which feels so real that you might forget it is a script. The dialogue is snappy and the awkward moments will definitely make you laugh if you have ever worked on a group project. While the plot is a bit circular and might feel slow to some, the honesty of the struggle is great. You should definitely check this out if you love stories about creative people failing upward.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that the cycle of chaos never really ends. As the crew struggles to finish their strange project, you realize that the process of making the show has become more important than the show itself. It ends on a note that shows how hard it is to actually satisfy an audience when your only goal is to document your own mistakes. It is a funny, honest look at artistic failure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves behind-the-scenes drama and indie comedies.
